connection_condition: atom.molecule_id corresponds to molecule.molecule_id; the molecule prefix of atom_id corresponds to the same value.
description: A molecule is composed of its atoms. An atom cannot exist without its owning molecule, and every atom in the dataset refers to a molecule.

connection_condition: bond.molecule_id corresponds to molecule.molecule_id; the molecule prefix of bond_id corresponds to the same value.
description: A molecule is composed of its bonds. A bond cannot exist without its owning molecule.
A bond is composed of its two atom-end connections; a connection record has no meaning without the bond it belongs to, and every bond yields exactly two connection records.

connection_condition: connected.atom_id and connected.atom_id2 correspond to atom.atom_id.
description: An atom participates in zero or more connections; each connection is an atom end of a bond and is meaningless without the atom it anchors.
A carcinogenic molecule is a molecule whose label marks it carcinogenic; the carcinogenic molecules are a proper subset of the molecule records that carry a label.
A non-carcinogenic molecule is a molecule whose label marks it as not carcinogenic; these form the complementary labelled subset.
An unbonded atom is a specific kind of atom: one whose atom identifier never appears in a connection record. It is a proper subset of all atoms.
A single bond is a specific kind of bond, distinguished by its bond type code; its value domain is a subset of all bonds.
A double bond is a specific kind of bond, distinguished by its bond type code; its value domain is a subset of all bonds.
A triple bond is a specific kind of bond, distinguished by its bond type code; it is the smallest bond-type subset in the dataset.

connection_condition: molecule.molecule_id, atom.molecule_id, bond.molecule_id and the TRnnn prefix of atom_id and bond_id all carry the same molecule key values.
description: The molecule key stored on the molecule record and the molecule key repeated on or embedded in structural records denote the same molecule; a molecule can therefore be reached from any structural record without joining through another identifier.
The atom count of a molecule is derived by counting its atoms, that is the number of atom records attributed to the molecule.
The atom number of an atom within its molecule is derived from its atom identifier by removing the molecule prefix, leaving the within-molecule position.
A bond type share is derived from bonds: it is the count of bonds of one bond type in a scope divided by the count of all bonds in the same scope.
An element share is derived from atoms: it is the count of atoms of one element in a scope divided by the count of all atoms in the same scope.
The majority bond type of a scope is derived from bonds by comparing how many bonds of each bond type the scope contains and selecting the largest group.
